summary: Extract Chrono Sedan TMeasy tyre + RWD driveline + load transfer; assess branchiness; design the branchless GPU port that closes the M1 longitudinal gap

result.role: TYRE + DRIVELINE EXTRACTOR — establishing the exact Chrono Sedan physics (TMeasy tyre + RWD driveline + powertrain) that produces the longitudinal force the GPU surrogate must reproduce
findings: CONSTRUCTION PATH: src/autodrift/chrono_vehicle_backend.py:625-635 builds the vehicle via the C++ wrapper veh.Sedan() (constructor_name='Sedan'), NOT the JSON Sedan.json. It calls SetTireType(TireModelType_TMEASY), SetTireStepSize(1e-3 s), SetContactMethod(NSC), then Initialize(). The wrapper class is chrono_models C++ (header /home/quyaonan/miniforge3/envs/chrono/include/chrono_models/vehicle/sedan/Sedan.h); its .cpp bodies are NOT shipped (binary install). However I instantiated the running objects in the chrono env and the C++ params match the shipped JSON data files exactly, so the JSONs are the authoritative readable spec.

VEHICLE (measured from running veh.Sedan()): total mass 1683.967 kg, chassis body mass 1515.0 kg (non-chassis = 168.97 kg; the backend overrides chassis mass to hit target total mass, see chrono_vehicle_backend.py:644-650). Wheelbase 2.776 m. Max steering angle 0.43633 rad (= 25 deg). Wheeltrack front 1.5958 m, rear 1.6 m. Chassis inertia XX=[222.8, 944.1, 1053.5] kg.m2 (Ixx,Iyy,Izz), COM at z=0.43 m. 2 axles, RWD (rear axle = driveline axle index 1).

TMEASY TYRE (template ChTMeasyTire, header /home/quyaonan/miniforge3/envs/chrono/include/chrono_vehicle/wheeled_vehicle/tire/ChTMeasyTire.h; JSON /home/quyaonan/miniforge3/envs/chrono/share/chrono/data/vehicle/sedan/tire/Sedan_TMeasyTire.json). DESIGN: Unloaded radius 0.3266 m, width 0.245 m, rim radius 0.2286 m, mass 11.5 kg, inertia [0.156,0.679,0.156]. Coefficient of Friction (reference mu_0) = 0.8. Rolling resistance coeff 0.015. Vehicle Type Passenger, Load Index 97. The force-curve coefficients are NOT in the JSON; they are derived at init by GuessPassCar70Par(loadIndex=97, width=0.245, ratio=0.70, rimDia=0.4572) which fills the TMeasyCoeff struct (dfx0, sxm, fxm, sxs, fxs at pn and 2*pn; same set for lateral fy). Standard Rill passenger-car-70pct parameter guess.

TMEASY MEASURED BEHAVIOR (full Sedan, flat terrain mu=0.8): static normal load per wheel ~4031 N front / ~4205 N rear (front axle share 0.489, near 50/50); total Fz 16474 N vs m*g 16520 N. Loaded radius R_eff 0.3237 m (front) / 0.3235 m (rear); deflection 8.83 mm at static load => vertical stiffness Cz ~ 4031/0.00883 ~ 456 kN/m. Longitudinal-slip sweep at full throttle: peak local Fx ~ 5500-5800 N at long-slip sx ~ 0.07-0.20 with Fz ~ 4000-5000 N, i.e. peak Fx/Fz ~ 1.2-1.4 (the effective-grip > mu*g noted in KNOWN_DIFFERENCES, chrono_vehicle_backend.py:128-130).

TMEASY FORCE MODEL (equations to port; bodies in template .cpp not shipped but algorithm is standard Rill TMeasy): (a) load-dependent curve via q = Fz/Fz_nom, with InterpL (linear, ChTMeasyTire.h:245) and InterpQ (quadratic, line 247) blending the pn and p2n coefficient sets; (b) per-axis force = tmxy_combined(f, fos, slip s, df0, sm, fm, ss, fs) (declared line 241) - the canonical TMeasy piecewise curve: initial slope df0 at s=0, rising to max fm at slip sm, then descending to sliding plateau fs at slip ss; (c) combined slip via CombinedCoulombForces(fx, fy, fz, muscale) (line 240) - couples Fx,Fy on the friction ellipse scaled by terrain mu (muscale = terrain_mu/mu_0 = terrain_mu/0.8); (d) standstill via Dahl/bristle friction (sigma0=1e5 bristle stiffness, sigma1=5000 damping, states brx/bry - lines 223-224,276-277) - the low-slip-velocity regularization that matters in the drift saddle; (e) normal force Fz = Cz*depth (linear m_d1) + damping; (f) effective rolling radius between unloaded 0.3266 and loaded ~0.3237.

ENGINE (Sedan_EngineSimpleMap, verified by instantiating veh.Sedan_EngineSimpleMap and probing GetOutputMotorshaftTorque vs GetMotorSpeed at full throttle - matches JSON /home/quyaonan/.../powertrain/Sedan_EngineSimpleMap.json EXACTLY). Max engine speed 6500 rpm (680.68 rad/s). Full-throttle torque map (rpm->Nm): 1000->236.8, 1400->338.3, 1600->370.0, FLAT 370.0 Nm from 1600 to 4500 rpm, then 5000->353.3, 5500->321.2, 6000->294.4, 6500->244.6. Zero-throttle (engine braking) map: 1500->-10, 3000->-15, 4500->-30, 5000->-50, 6000->-70, 6500->-100 Nm. EngineSimpleMap is power+torque limited, no torque converter, instantaneous in the SIMPLE_MAP path.

TRANSMISSION (Sedan_AutomaticTransmissionSimpleMap, JSON .../powertrain/Sedan_AutomaticTransmissionSimpleMap.json; verified running). 6 forward gear ratios [0.265, 0.489, 0.784, 1.063, 1.276, 1.499], reverse -0.333. Chrono convention: output torque = engine_torque / gear_ratio (small ratio = large torque multiplication). Shift points (down,up rpm per gear): 1st[1000,4000], 2nd[1200,4500], 3rd[1400,4500], 4th[1600,4500], 5th[1800,4500], 6th[2000,4500]. Auto shift: upshift when motor rpm exceeds the gear up-point, downshift below its down-point. NO torque converter. Measured launch: shifts 1->4 within ~2.5 s, holds engine 3000-4500 rpm. (Despite the backend docstring saying 4-speed, the actual map has 6 forward gears.)

DRIVELINE (Sedan_Driveline2WD, template ChShaftsDriveline2WD, JSON .../driveline/Sedan_Driveline2WD.json). RWD: drives suspension index [1] = rear axle only (Sedan_Vehicle.json 'Suspension Indexes':[1]). Final drive Conical Gear ratio 0.2 (=> further 5x torque multiplication; T_axle = T_driveshaft/0.2). Driveshaft inertia 0.5 kg.m2, differential box inertia 0.6 kg.m2. Open differential with Axle Differential Locking Limit 100 N.m (bias a locked diff can carry; effectively open for drift). VERIFIED end-to-end: at 1750 rpm in gear 1, engine 370 Nm -> driveshaft torque 1397.86 Nm = 370/0.265, then /0.2 conical -> ~6989 Nm split across 2 rear wheels.

THROTTLE/BRAKE -> WHEEL TORQUE -> LONGITUDINAL FORCE CHAIN: backend feeds DriverInputs m_throttle in [0,1] (chrono_vehicle_backend.py:538) into EngineSimpleMap: T_eng = (1-throttle)*map0(rpm) + throttle*mapF(rpm). T_eng -> /gear_ratio -> /0.2 conical -> open diff splits to 2 rear wheels -> wheel spin accelerates -> long slip sx develops -> TMeasy tmxy_combined returns Fx. BRAKE: m_braking in [0,1] (line 539) -> Sedan_BrakeSimple applies brake torque to ALL 4 wheels (simple proportional), opposing wheel spin. The backend ALSO pre-shapes throttle/brake through an AutoDrift first-order actuator lag (drive_tau, brake) at the 50 Hz layer (chrono_vehicle_backend.py:787-809) IN ADDITION to Chrono's own dynamics (double shaping, KNOWN_DIFFERENCES line 137-138).

STEERING MAP: Sedan_RackPinion (steering/Sedan_RackPinion.json), pinion radius 0.3, max pinion angle 15.5 deg, rack-pinion converts steering input to road-wheel angle. Vehicle GetMaxSteeringAngle()=25 deg=0.43633 rad at full lock. Backend: normalized steer command in [-1,1] maps full-scale -> full lock (chrono_vehicle_backend.py:536, inputs.m_steering = steer_state/max_steer clamped). AutoDrift max_steer is 0.62 rad, so physical steer gain ~0.70x (KNOWN_DIFFERENCES line 134-135). Front-wheel angle = m_steering * 0.43633 rad.

TERRAIN/FRICTION: veh.FlatTerrain(0.0, mu) - flat plane at z=0 with uniform friction mu (chrono_vehicle_backend.py:703). Scenario mu enters TMeasy as muscale = mu/mu_0 = mu/0.8 scaling the friction-ellipse force caps. Friction step swaps the terrain object to a new mu mid-episode (line 821).

branchy_parts.what: Auto-transmission gear selection (discrete state: current gear 1-6, with up/downshift thresholds on engine rpm)
branchy_parts.why_branchy: Each env has an integer current-gear state and shifts when rpm crosses a per-gear threshold - an if/elif ladder per env per step plus a stateful discrete variable, the classic branch that breaks SIMT batching across N envs.
branchy_parts.branchless_plan: Represent current_gear as an int tensor [N]. Build gear-ratio LUT [6] and shift-band tensors up[6]/down[6]. Each step: ratio = gather(ratios, gear); rpm = wheel_omega * ratio_total * 60/2pi; upshift = (rpm > gather(up,gear)) & (gear<5); downshift = (rpm < gather(down,gear)) & (gear>0); gear = gear + upshift.int() - downshift.int(). All gather/compare/add vectorized, zero Python branches. Optionally add shift dwell as a counter tensor.

branchy_parts.what: EngineSimpleMap full/zero-throttle torque interpolation over the rpm breakpoint table
branchy_parts.why_branchy: Piecewise-linear interpolation does a per-sample bin search (which segment is rpm in?) - naively a loop/branch per env.
branchy_parts.branchless_plan: torch.searchsorted on the sorted rpm-breakpoint tensor finds the bin for the whole [N] batch, then vectorized linear interp T = T0 + (T1-T0)*(rpm-r0)/(r1-r0). Blend: T_eng = (1-throttle)*map0(rpm) + throttle*mapF(rpm). Fully batched, no branches.

branchy_parts.what: TMeasy tmxy_combined piecewise force curve (rising branch to fm at sm, descending to sliding plateau fs at ss)
branchy_parts.why_branchy: The curve is defined region-by-region in the slip variable (0<s<sm rising; sm<s<ss descending; s>ss flat), classically coded as if/elif on s.
branchy_parts.branchless_plan: Compute each region closed form over the whole [N,4] tensor (N envs x 4 wheels), select with torch.where masks: f = where(s<sm, rise(s), where(s<ss, fall(s), fs_plateau)). All three branches computed densely and masked - standard branchless GPU technique, ~3x arithmetic but fully SIMT.

branchy_parts.what: Combined-slip friction ellipse coupling (CombinedCoulombForces) and load interpolation q=Fz/Fz_nom (InterpL linear vs InterpQ quadratic)
branchy_parts.why_branchy: Combined slip caps |F| on an ellipse and reallocates Fx/Fy by slip direction; the load blend chooses linear vs quadratic depending on q<1 vs q>1.
branchy_parts.branchless_plan: Compute combined slip s_comb = sqrt((sx/sxm)^2+(sy/sym)^2) densely; scale fx,fy by the ellipse factor (vectorized). For the load blend compute BOTH InterpL and InterpQ over the batch and select with where(q<1, linL, quadQ) - both simple polynomials in q. No data-dependent control flow.

branchy_parts.what: TMeasy standstill / Dahl bristle friction (sigma0=1e5, sigma1=5000, bristle states brx,bry) at near-zero slip velocity
branchy_parts.why_branchy: TMeasy switches between the sliding-curve regime and a bristle/Dahl stick regime below a velocity threshold (vcoulomb/vnum) and integrates bristle deflection ODEs - a per-env regime branch plus extra state.
branchy_parts.branchless_plan: Carry bristle deflection state tensors brx,bry [N,4]. Compute both stick and slip force densely and blend with a smooth velocity weight w = clamp(|v_slip|/vcoulomb,0,1) via where/lerp instead of a hard switch. Lowest-confidence part (governs the drift saddle where slip velocity is small); needs validation against scripts/feasibility_audit/surrogate_m1_divergence.py traces and matching Chrono vcoulomb/vnum thresholds.

branchy_parts.what: Brake-vs-drive arbitration and actuator-lag pre-shaping (drive_force_state sign decides throttle vs brake)
branchy_parts.why_branchy: chrono_vehicle_backend.py:806-809 picks throttle OR brake from the sign of drive_force_state - a per-env branch.
branchy_parts.branchless_plan: throttle = relu(drive_force_state)/max_drive; brake = relu(-drive_force_state)/max_brake - branchless via relu. The first-order lag (drive_tau, steer_tau) is a vectorizable EMA; the steer rate limit is a clamp/where on the delta, trivially batched.

result.effort_estimate: 2-4 weeks for a validated branchless GPU port of THIS force model. (1) Engine map + 6-speed auto-shift + driveline torque chain to rear-wheel torque: ~3-4 days, mostly mechanical (searchsorted interp + gather-based gear FSM); the gear FSM with hysteresis is the only fiddly part. (2) TMeasy longitudinal+lateral curves (tmxy_combined, load blend q, combined-slip ellipse): ~1 week; equations are standard Rill TMeasy and the GuessPassCar70Par coefficients are deterministic from (LI=97, width 0.245, ratio 0.70, rim 0.4572), but the shipped tmxy_combined .cpp body is not readable, so the exact piecewise form must be reconstructed from Rill's published equations and validated numerically against ReportTireForce sweeps (the probe harness built in this task already works and yields ground-truth Fx/Fy(slip,Fz)). (3) GENUINELY HARD: the TMeasy standstill/Dahl bristle regime and low-slip-velocity blend - exactly the drift-saddle regime where M1 measured divergence; Chrono's vcoulomb/vnum thresholds + bristle ODE must be matched, not approximated - budget ~1 week of validation iteration. (4) Wheel-spin / driveline rotational DOF: M1 says the gap is longitudinal, so wheel angular dynamics (T_wheel - R*Fx = I_wheel*omega_dot, with driveshaft/diff inertia 0.5+0.6 kg.m2) must be integrated per wheel - adds 4 (or lumped rear) rotational states per env; ~2-3 days but it is the state the current SingleTrackDriftModel lacks and the likely root of the vx RMSE. Quasi-static load transfer (front/rear Fz split + transfer from ax,ay) is cheap (~1-2 days, closed form). Total realistic: 3 weeks single-engineer, 4 weeks with thorough Chrono validation across the scenario envelope.
result.recommendation: Port in this dependency order, validating each layer against the working Chrono probe harness (the /tmp probes in this task extract ground truth - fold them into scripts/feasibility_audit/surrogate_m1_divergence.py): (1) FIRST add the missing wheel/driveline rotational DOF and the EngineSimpleMap -> 6-speed-auto -> conical-0.2 -> open-diff torque chain to the rear wheels. M1 says the dominant gap is longitudinal vx (~1.1 m/s RMSE); the current SingleTrackDriftModel almost certainly applies a static drive FORCE and has no wheel-spin / engine-torque / gear state, so the slip-driven Fx is wrong during throttle transients - this single layer likely closes most of the gap. (2) THEN replace the simple drive-force-to-Fx with the real TMeasy longitudinal curve (tmxy_combined + load blend + combined-slip ellipse), using GuessPassCar70Par-derived coefficients calibrated to match the ReportTireForce(slip,Fz) sweep numerically rather than re-deriving symbolically. (3) Keep the existing lateral/yaw model but feed it TMeasy Fy (lateral gap already moderate ~0.25/0.17). (4) LAST, tune the standstill/Dahl low-slip-velocity blend against drift-saddle traces - the only part likely to need iteration. All six branchy parts have clean branchless plans (searchsorted, gather, where/relu), so the model is fully GPU-batchable; nothing requires the multibody constraint solver, confirming the M1 decision direction. KEY VALUES to hardcode: mu_0=0.8; gear ratios [0.265,0.489,0.784,1.063,1.276,1.499] + rev -0.333; conical final drive 0.2; engine peak 370 Nm flat 1600-4500 rpm, max 6500 rpm; R_eff~0.3237 m; Cz~456 kN/m; static axle split 0.489/0.511; max_steer 0.4363 rad; wheelbase 2.776 m; total mass 1684 kg (chassis 1515 + non-chassis 169); driveshaft+diff inertia 0.5+0.6 kg.m2.

result.role: Branchiness + GPU-port assessor for the TMeasy tyre + ShaftsDriveline2WD (RWD) + load-transfer force model
findings: MODEL IDENTITY (data files): the Chrono Sedan force model is fixed by JSON at /home/quyaonan/miniforge3/envs/chrono/share/chrono/data/vehicle/sedan/. Tyre = TMeasyTire (Sedan_TMeasyTire.json: R=0.3266m, mu_ref=0.8, rr=0.015, LoadIndex=97); driveline = ShaftsDriveline2WD (RWD, conical 0.2, diff-box inertia 0.6, driveshaft inertia 0.5, diff-locking-limit 100 N·m); engine = EngineSimpleMap (flat 370 N·m plateau 1500-4500 rpm, max 6500); transmission = AutomaticTransmissionSimpleMap (6 fwd gears [0.265,0.489,0.784,1.063,1.276,1.499], shift bands ~[1000-2000 down, 4000-4500 up], NO torque converter); brakes = BrakeSimple (constant torque ∝ modulation, ODE-friendly speed-dependent, no set-valued constraint).

THE M1 LONGITUDINAL GAP IS A MISSING STATE, NOT A MISSING BRANCH. The current GPU surrogate (src/autodrift/gpu_surrogate.py) models rear long. force as fx_rear = clamp(drive_force, ±0.98·mu·Fzr) — drive_force is a first-order-lagged command, NOT a tyre force. Chrono's TMeasy computes Fx from longitudinal SLIP sx = -(vx - omega·R_eff)/vta, where omega (wheel spin) is an integrated driveline state. The dominant vx RMSE ~1.1 m/s is precisely this: the surrogate has no wheel-spin/driveline state, so it cannot reproduce drive-force buildup, wheel spin-up under drift, or engine/gear torque limiting. This is the #1 thing to add and it is a STATE addition (per-env scalars), fully branchless.

TMeasy force law (from ChTMeasyTire.cpp, header ChTMeasyTire.h): tmxy_combined(s,df0,sm,fm,ss,fs) is a PIECEWISE curve with 3-4 regimes: (a) s>ss => f=fs (pure sliding); (b) s<sm => rational adhesion f=df0·sm·sn/(1+(sn+p)·sn); (c) sm<=s<=ss => two-parabola or cubic blend depending on sstar<=ss. Combined slip: sc=hypot(sx,sy), project params onto (calpha=sx/sc, salpha=sy/sc), evaluate the scalar curve once, then Fx=f·calpha, Fy=f·salpha. Load interpolation q=clamp(Fz,0,pn_max)/pn with InterpL (linear, q in [1,2]) and InterpQ (quadratic) blends of per-load coefficients.

GENUINE STATEFUL/ITERATIVE PIECES (3): (1) wheel-spin omega per axle — ODE state driven by drive torque minus tyre Fx·R minus brake torque; (2) TMeasy slip-state / Dahl bristle deformation brx,bry at standstill — small linear-implicit (BDF1 or trapezoidal) update, already a closed-form 1-step solve in Chrono (no fixed-point loop); (3) ShaftsDriveline2WD is a 4-shaft / 3-constraint 1D linear system (conical gear + planetary differential Willis ratio -1 + optional locking clutch) — in Chrono solved by the NSC solver, but for an OPEN differential it reduces to a small fixed linear system solvable in closed form / one batched 3x3 solve, NO data-dependent iteration.

LOAD TRANSFER: the Sedan has double-wishbone (front) + multilink (rear) suspensions, i.e. real compliant multibody suspension with its own DOFs. M1 reports lateral/yaw gap is only moderate (~0.25 m/s vy, ~0.17 rad/s yaw) and the gap is dominantly longitudinal, which means quasi-static algebraic load transfer (Fz_i = static + longitudinal·(h/L) + lateral·(h/track)) is very likely sufficient — the full suspension ODE is NOT required (consistent with the M1 conclusion that the multibody constraint solver isn't where the gap lives). Quasi-static load transfer is pure algebra, fully branchless (only clamp Fz>=0).

STANDSTILL / CONTACT branches that DO change the model if smoothed: (a) TMeasy in_contact (depth<=0 => zero force) — on flat terrain the tyre is always in contact during driving, so this branch is effectively constant and can be dropped/masked with zero downstream effect; (b) Dahl standstill friction + frblend (ChFunctionSineStep over vx in [frblend_begin,frblend_end]) handles vx near 0 — drift episodes run at 5-12 m/s so this regime is never visited; it can be replaced by the high-speed slip branch (matches the surrogate's existing vx_safe>=0.75 guard). (c) startup transition (sinestep over time) only affects t<~0.5s after Initialize — the spin-up handoff already passes this, so irrelevant at episode start.

GEAR-SHIFT IS ACTUALLY EXERCISED (computed): at wheel R=0.3266 and conical 0.2, motor RPM crosses shift thresholds inside the 5-12 m/s band — gear 1->2 near ~9 m/s, gear 2->3 near ~12 m/s; and because the rear wheel SPINS UP in a drift, omega>>v/R drives engine RPM even higher, triggering dynamic upshifts. So m_current_gear is a genuine path-dependent integer state with hysteresis (down/up thresholds differ). This is the only true hysteretic discrete state in the model.

BRANCH INVENTORY (algebraic, trivially maskable with torch.where/clamp, NO parity change): action clamps; throttle/brake sign split (drive_force>=0 ? throttle:brake); vx_safe sign/min guard (already in surrogate via torch.where); fx friction-circle clamp; sqrt(max(.,1.0)) capacity floors; atan2 slip angles; engine torque = (1-thr)·map0(rpm)+thr·mapF(rpm) with rpm clamp [0,6500] (maps are 1D interp => torch.searchsorted/bucketize, batched, branchless); motor_speed=|driveshaft_speed|/gear_ratio; driveshaft_torque=motor_torque/gear_ratio; tmxy piecewise curve (select regime per-env with torch.where over the 3-4 closed-form expressions — each env evaluates its branch via masking, exact, no smoothing needed).

branchy_parts.what: Automatic gear selection: m_current_gear integer with hysteresis (upshift if motor_rpm > shift_up[gear], downshift if motor_rpm < shift_down[gear]). Confirmed exercised in the 5-12 m/s drift band, plus dynamic upshifts when the rear wheel spins up.
branchy_parts.why_branchy: Genuinely data-dependent discrete state with hysteresis: which gear an env is in depends on its RPM history, so envs diverge into different gear ratios on the same control step. The shift is an instantaneous ratio jump (discontinuous), not a smooth function. Smoothing it (e.g. a continuous effective ratio) WOULD change the model and break bit-parity, because the engine torque map output jumps when the ratio jumps.
branchy_parts.branchless_plan: Keep gear as an int64 per-env state tensor g[N]. Each step compute up = motor_rpm > shift_up.gather(g) & g<5; down = motor_rpm < shift_down.gather(g) & g>0; g = g + up.long() - down.long() (at most one step/control-tick, matching Chrono). gear_ratio = ratios.gather(g). This is pure gather + comparison + integer add — fully branchless and BIT-EXACT to Chrono's hysteresis (no smoothing). Cost: a few [N] ops. The discontinuity is preserved exactly; it is not a smoothing approximation, it is masked selection. This is the textbook case where the user's thesis holds: the 'branch' is just data-parallel state selection.

branchy_parts.what: TMeasy piecewise slip->force curve tmxy_combined (3-4 regimes selected by s vs sm, s vs ss, sstar vs ss).
branchy_parts.why_branchy: Per-env the slip magnitude sc lands in a different regime (adhesion rational / parabola / cubic / pure-slide), so envs take different algebraic branches. Naively this looks like control-flow divergence.
branchy_parts.branchless_plan: Each regime is a closed-form expression of the SAME inputs. Compute all 3-4 expressions unconditionally for every env, then select with nested torch.where on the regime masks (s>ss, s<sm, sstar<=ss). No iteration, no smoothing, exact parity. The wasted FLOPs (computing 4 branches, using 1) are negligible and fully GPU-friendly. The only care item: guard divisions (sc, vta, df0) with eps so the unused branches don't produce NaN that poisons the where (standard masked-NaN hygiene).

branchy_parts.what: Wheel-spin omega ODE + open-differential 1D shaft coupling (driveshaft/diffbox/L+R axles, 3 constraints) + Dahl bristle standstill update.
branchy_parts.why_branchy: In Chrono these are resolved by the NSC multibody/constraint solver, which feels 'iterative'. The concern is whether porting needs an env-dependent iterative solve.
branchy_parts.branchless_plan: It does NOT. For an OPEN differential the constraint set is FIXED (no contact set-changes at the speeds involved), so it is one small constant-structure linear system per env: solve a 2-3 DOF system in closed form (or a batched torch.linalg.solve on a [N,3,3]) every step — same structure for all envs => no divergence. The diff-locking clutch (limit 100 N·m, tiny) can be modeled as open (negligible) or as a clamped torque torch.clamp(±100) — branchless. omega integrated with the same fixed-step RK4/semi-implicit Euler the surrogate already uses. Dahl standstill is Chrono's own closed-form linear-implicit 1-step update (brx = (fc·brx + fc·h·vsx)/(fc + h·sigma0·|vsx|)) — already non-iterative, directly portable as elementwise ops; and at 5-12 m/s it is never the active regime anyway.

branchy_parts.what: Engine/brake/contact regime guards: in_contact (depth<=0), frblend/startup sinesteps near vx≈0, throttle/brake sign split, friction-circle clamp.
branchy_parts.why_branchy: These are if/else in the C++ but only one side is ever taken in the operating regime (always in contact on flat terrain; always above the standstill blend speed during a drift; throttle XOR brake by sign).
branchy_parts.branchless_plan: All collapse to torch.where/clamp with zero parity cost because the OTHER branch is never visited in-distribution: in_contact -> assume true (flat terrain), drop the branch; frblend/startup sinestep -> evaluate the sinestep formula (it saturates to 1.0 above frblend_end, so it's a clamp/where, and =1 in the whole drift regime); throttle/brake -> torque = throttle·Tmax_drive(rpm,gear) - brake·Tbrake (both terms, brake side zero when throttle>0 by construction); friction circle -> the existing clamp/sqrt(max(.,eps)) pattern already in gpu_surrogate.py. None of these change the model in the visited regime.

result.effort_estimate: 2-4 weeks for a torch-batched, branchless port that closes the M1 longitudinal gap to parity, NOT months. Breakdown: (1) ~3-4 days to add per-env wheel-spin omega + algebraic open-differential split + EngineSimpleMap torque map (1D bucketize) + hysteretic integer gear state — this alone should kill most of the 1.1 m/s vx gap because it introduces the missing drive-force/slip physics; (2) ~3-4 days to port tmxy_combined as masked closed-form regimes + load-q interpolation + quasi-static load transfer to replace the tanh saturation tyre; (3) ~1 week validation/tuning against Chrono via scripts/feasibility_audit/surrogate_m1_divergence.py (extend it to log vx/omega/gear, sweep the drift saddle, drive p90 beta-div past the >=24-step gate). The GENUINELY HARD parts are NOT branches: (a) the TMeasy per-load coefficient set (dfx0, fxm, sxm, fym, sym, ...) is NOT in the JSON — it is auto-guessed at runtime from LoadIndex=97 via GuessPassCar70Par(); you must reproduce that guess table (read it out of a live Chrono tire once and hardcode, or replicate GuessPassCar70Par) or your curve shape won't match. (b) matching Fz quasi-static load transfer to Chrono's compliant double-wishbone/multilink steady state may need a 1-2 parameter calibration (effective CG height / roll stiffness split). (c) exact bit-parity is impossible (different integrator/solver), so the target is statistical trajectory parity (RMSE/beta-div gate), which is the right bar for a PPO surrogate anyway.
result.recommendation: PROCEED with the branchless GPU port — the user's thesis is essentially correct FOR THIS FORCE MODEL. There is exactly ONE genuinely data-dependent, hysteretic discrete branch (automatic gear selection), and it is bit-exactly maskable as integer per-env state selection (gather + compare + int-add), NOT something you must smooth. Every other 'branch' is either (i) a closed-form regime selectable with torch.where at zero parity cost (TMeasy piecewise curve, sign/clamp guards), or (ii) a branch whose other side is never visited in the 5-12 m/s drift regime (in_contact, standstill Dahl/frblend, startup transition) and can be dropped. Critically, the M1 longitudinal gap is NOT a branchiness problem at all — it is a MISSING STATE (wheel spin omega + driveline torque path), which is fully branchless to add (per-env scalars + one fixed-structure small linear solve). The real blockers are data/calibration, not control flow: (1) recovering TMeasy's runtime-guessed per-load tyre coefficients from LoadIndex=97 (extract from a live Chrono tire, ~half a day), and (2) calibrating quasi-static load transfer against the compliant suspension's steady state. Neither blocks the GPU vectorization. CONCRETE NEXT STEP: extend scripts/feasibility_audit/surrogate_m1_divergence.py to also dump Chrono wheel omega, longitudinal slip, normal loads per wheel, and current gear (the backend already collects tire telemetry incl. GetLongitudinalSlip/GetTireOmega in _collect_tire_telemetry_from_vehicle), then prototype the omega+driveline state addition first and re-measure vx RMSE — that single addition is the highest-leverage, lowest-risk change and will confirm the diagnosis before investing in the full TMeasy curve."

result.role: LOAD-TRANSFER + VALIDATION designer (AutoDrift Path B GPU surrogate)
findings: Operating envelope (from scripts/feasibility_audit/phase4_e4_drift_regime_pricing.py:214-238 and phase4_f2_train.py:140-141): DRIFT saddle cell `low_mu_power_oversteer` = mu=0.48, speed=9.0 m/s, initial_beta=0.22 rad, R=70 m; second cell `lift_off_recovery` mu=0.55, 8 m/s, beta=-0.28, R=60. AVOIDANCE regime spans mu in {0.3625,0.5875,0.8125,1.0375}. The load-transfer model must hold across mu 0.36-1.04 and ay up to ~mu*g.

Chrono Sedan geometry (the params the load-transfer model needs), read from the JSON data files under /home/quyaonan/miniforge3/envs/chrono/share/chrono/data/vehicle/sedan/: wheelbase L=2.776 m (Sedan_Vehicle.json:39); suspension front at x=+1.388, rear x=-1.388 (Sedan_Vehicle.json:13,23) => symmetric, lf=lr=1.388 m, STATIC 50/50 axle split (the single-track at lf=1.35/lr=1.45 is NOT 50/50 — a mapping mismatch); half-track = spindle COM y = 0.7979 m (Sedan_DoubleWishbone.json:11) => track width t≈1.596 m; chassis mass 1550 kg, chassis centroid z=0.7 in chassis frame (Sedan_Chassis.json:9-13); tire unloaded radius 0.3266 m, mu_ref=0.8 (Sedan_TMeasyTire.json).

CG height: backend measures equilibrium ride height ref-frame z≈0.2145 m (chrono_vehicle_backend.py:80). Mass-weighting the 1550 kg chassis (CG≈0.91 m above ground) against ~119 kg of unsprung mass (CG≈0.31 m, hub height) gives a full-vehicle h_cg≈0.87 m — substantially higher than the single-track default h_cg=0.52 (dynamics.py:24). h_cg must NOT be assumed; it must be CALIBRATED against Chrono's per-wheel normal loads (effective transfer is reduced by suspension anti-dive/anti-squat geometry and the ref-frame offset).

Load-transfer magnitude at the drift saddle (mu=0.48, m=1684, h_cg≈0.87, t≈1.60, L=2.776): static per-axle load ≈8260 N; lateral transfer dFz=m*ay*h/t ≈ 4329 N ≈ 52% of axle load; longitudinal transfer dFz=m*ax*h/L ≈ 2489 N ≈ 30% of axle load. These are first-order effects the surrogate's STATIC fzf/fzr (gpu_surrogate.py:49-54) entirely ignores — directly explaining why the rear saturates at the wrong step in the drift saddle.

KEY DISAMBIGUATION of the M1 longitudinal gap: the vx RMSE ~1.1 m/s is driveline-shaped, NOT load-transfer-shaped. Chrono drive force at 9 m/s is engine-torque-curve x gear x conical(0.2)/r_wheel: 3rd gear≈7600 N, 4th≈5600 N (Sedan_AutomaticTransmissionSimpleMap.json forward ratios [0.265,0.489,0.784,1.063,1.276,1.499], EngineSimpleMap peak ~370 Nm, Driveline2WD conical 0.2). The surrogate uses a FLAT 8200 N cap (dynamics.py:31). Load transfer modulates the GRIP ENVELOPE (mu*Fz, i.e. when the rear breaks away); the driveline modulates the FORCE DELIVERED. Both feed vx but fix different things — load transfer alone will not close vx RMSE.

Validation ground truth already exists and is free: chrono_vehicle_backend.py:368-425 `_collect_tire_telemetry_from_vehicle` emits per-wheel `normal_load_n` (Fz), `local_force_x_n` (Fx), `local_force_y_n` (Fy), `slip_angle_rad`, `longitudinal_slip` into diagnostics, and the worker forwards diagnostics as step `info` (chrono_backend_worker.py:89,103,117). So the surrogate's per-wheel Fz can be validated DIRECTLY against Chrono per wheel, not just via the downstream vx/beta trajectory.

TMeasy is load-dependent and degressive (the reason static loads fail): ChTMeasyTire.h:200-249 interpolates ALL force coefficients (dfx0, fxm, fym, ...) between nominal load pn and 2*pn via q=Fz/Fz_nom using InterpL (linear) / InterpQ (quadratic, sub-linear). So peak lateral/longitudinal force grows SUB-linearly with Fz — a loaded outer tire gains less grip than an unloaded inner tire loses. A single-track that sums two wheels at static load overestimates total axle grip; modeling per-wheel Fz with a degressive mu*Fz envelope captures this.

M1 has NOT been re-run to capture stored numbers: runs/feasibility_audit/phase4_f2/m1_div_stderr.log is empty (0 bytes), and no `vx_rmse` appears in any runs/ artifact. The thresholds in surrogate_m1_divergence.py:99-101 (median cross step >=24, mean beta@24 p90<=0.03) are the gate of record; the script must be the validation harness, extended to log per-step vx/vy/yaw RMSE and per-wheel Fz error.

branchy_parts.what: Per-wheel normal-load assignment: which axle/side gets +dFz vs -dFz depends on the signs of ax and ay (4 sign combinations), and the inner/outer wheel split flips with turn direction.
branchy_parts.why_branchy: A naive implementation is `if ay>0: outer=left ...` with nested if/else over ax/ay signs and per-wheel branches — 4-8 branches that destroy GPU warp coherence across N envs that drift in different directions.
branchy_parts.branchless_plan: Compute signed transfers and add them with fixed per-wheel sign vectors, no conditionals. Fz_FL = Fz_static_f - 0.5*dFz_long - 0.5*dFz_lat_f; Fz_FR = Fz_static_f - 0.5*dFz_long + 0.5*dFz_lat_f; rear analogously with +0.5*dFz_long. Here dFz_long = m*ax*h_cg/L (signed by ax) and dFz_lat_axle = m*ay*h_cg/t * load_dist_axle (signed by ay). The sign of ay automatically routes transfer to the correct side because dFz_lat enters with a +/- constant per wheel and ay carries the sign. All four Fz are pure arithmetic on [N] tensors — fully branchless, warp-coherent.

branchy_parts.what: Normal-load positivity / wheel-lift clamp: at mu near 1.0 and high ay, inner-wheel Fz can go negative (wheel lift), which must be clamped to >=0.
branchy_parts.why_branchy: `torch.where(Fz<0, 0, Fz)` is fine, but the physically-correct response (redistribute the lost load to the outer wheel to conserve axle vertical force) tempts a branch / iterative solve.
branchy_parts.branchless_plan: Use Fz = torch.clamp(Fz, min=Fz_floor) with a small positive floor (e.g. 1.0 N, matching the existing clamp style at gpu_surrogate.py:91-93). For the drift saddle (mu<=0.55) wheel-lift does not occur, so axle-load conservation is second-order; defer the redistribute-to-outer term as an optional branchless correction (add the clamped-off deficit to the paired wheel via a fixed pairing index) only if avoidance-regime (mu~1.04) validation shows it matters. Keep the clamp, skip the redistribution in v1.

branchy_parts.what: Combined-slip grip envelope per wheel using the load-dependent (degressive) mu*Fz, replacing the current static rear_capacity (gpu_surrogate.py:88-96).
branchy_parts.why_branchy: Replicating TMeasy's q=Fz/Fz_nom regime (InterpL below 2*pn, extrapolate above) invites `if q<=2: InterpL else clamp` branches per wheel.
branchy_parts.branchless_plan: Approximate TMeasy's degressive load dependence with a single smooth closed form: peak_force(Fz) = mu * Fz * (1 - k_deg*(Fz/Fz_nom - 1)), with Fz_nom = static axle/2 and k_deg a small fitted degressivity constant (~0.05-0.15), all clamped via torch.clamp — no regime branch. Keep the existing tanh combined-slip saturation shape (gpu_surrogate.py:95-96) but feed it the per-wheel load-dependent capacity. q is just Fz/Fz_nom, a division; the degressive term is one multiply. Fully vectorised.

branchy_parts.what: Optional first-order roll/pitch lag: transfer responds to ay/ax through suspension compliance with a ~50-150 ms time constant rather than instantaneously (quasi-static).
branchy_parts.why_branchy: Tempts an inner sub-step loop or stiff-ODE special-casing; a stateful lag adds 2 hidden state channels and an `if use_lag` config branch.
branchy_parts.branchless_plan: Implement as two extra exponential-filter state channels (filtered_ay, filtered_ax) updated each control step with the SAME branchless first-order filter already used for the actuator states (gpu_surrogate.py:150,157: alpha=clamp(dt/max(tau,dt),0,1)). Feed the filtered accelerations into the transfer equations instead of instantaneous ax/ay. Add 2 to STATE_DIM (8->10). One filter constant tau_roll; if validation shows quasi-static is sufficient, set tau_roll=0 (alpha=1) which collapses to instantaneous with zero branch cost. Decide via ablation, not at runtime.

branchy_parts.what: ax/ay source for the transfer (chicken-and-egg): transfer depends on tire forces, which depend on Fz, which depends on transfer.
branchy_parts.why_branchy: A fixed-point / implicit solve per step invites a while-loop-until-converged, which is variable-iteration and warp-divergent.
branchy_parts.branchless_plan: Break the loop explicitly: use the PREVIOUS RK4 substage's body accelerations (ax_body=vx_dot - yaw_rate*vy ... already computed at gpu_surrogate.py:116-117) to set Fz for the CURRENT tire-force eval. Within one RK4 step this is a single explicit pass (compute accel from stage k_{i-1}, set Fz, eval forces) — no iteration. Equivalently, evaluate transfer once at the start of each control step from the last step's accelerations (quasi-static, 50 Hz lag is negligible vs the 0.5-1.0 m/s gap). Zero branches, fixed cost.

result.effort_estimate: 2-3 weeks for the load-transfer piece in isolation; ~4-6 weeks for the full physics rewrite that actually closes the M1 gap, because load transfer is necessary but NOT sufficient. Breakdown: (1) Load-transfer model + per-wheel Fz + degressive grip envelope in gpu_surrogate.py: ~3-4 days to write branchlessly, ~3-4 days to calibrate h_cg/k_deg against Chrono tire_telemetry. GENUINELY HARD part: the dominant M1 gap is LONGITUDINAL/driveline (flat 8200 N cap vs gear+torque-curve force that is ~5600-7600 N at 9 m/s and rpm-dependent) — closing vx RMSE needs a branchless driveline surrogate (engine torque map -> gear selection -> wheel force) layered alongside, ~1-2 weeks, and gear-selection is the worst branchy hazard (discrete shift logic). The TMeasy degressive-load fit (matching Chrono's InterpL/InterpQ regime) without the actual .cpp coefficients (not shipped in the conda binary) requires fitting from Chrono telemetry sweeps, ~3-5 days. Risk: even with both, a thin learned residual may still be needed for the lateral/yaw ~0.25/0.17 gap (suspension kinematics, camber, relaxation length) — budget 1 week contingency.
result.recommendation:
IMPLEMENT in src/autodrift/gpu_surrogate.py in this order, validating each piece against Chrono telemetry before the next. (A) LOAD TRANSFER, branchless: add params h_cg, track_width to PARAM_KEYS and ParamBatch (currently absent; gpu_surrogate.py:32-36 has no h_cg/track); set lf=lr=1.388 / track=1.596 / wheelbase=2.776 / h_cg as a CALIBRATED free param seeded at ~0.6 (between geometric 0.87 and current 0.52). Replace static fzf/fzr (gpu_surrogate.py:49-54) with a `_normal_loads(ax_body, ay_body, P)` returning [N,4] per-wheel Fz via the branchless signed-transfer formula. (B) Make the grip envelope load-dependent: feed per-wheel mu*Fz (with the degressive (1-k_deg*(q-1)) factor) into the rear/front capacity instead of the static mu*fzr (gpu_surrogate.py:88-96); the single-track collapses the two wheels of an axle by SUMMING their load-dependent capacities (this is what captures the sub-linear axle-grip loss). (C) Source ax/ay from the previous RK4 stage's accelerations (explicit, no fixed-point). (D) Optional roll/pitch lag as 2 filtered-accel state channels (STATE_DIM 8->10) reusing the existing first-order filter; ablate tau_roll, default to quasi-static. 

TEST each piece against Chrono via an EXTENDED surrogate_m1_divergence.py: (1) NEW UNIT-LEVEL check — at each step compare the surrogate's per-wheel Fz against Chrono diagnostics `tire_telemetry[*].normal_load_n` (front-axle sum, rear-axle sum, and lateral L/R split); target per-axle Fz RMSE < 10% of static axle load and CORRECT SIGN of the L/R split. This isolates the load-transfer model from the driveline. (2) Then the existing trajectory gate (surrogate_m1_divergence.py:99-101): median step where |beta| crosses 0.03 rad >= 24, mean beta@24 with p90 <= 0.03 rad, AND add vx RMSE logging (already computed at line 91, just not gated). 

DECISION RULE: 'physics rewrite closed the gap' iff, on >=8 seeds at the drift saddle, beta@24 p90 <= 0.03 rad AND vx RMSE <= 0.4 m/s AND per-axle Fz RMSE < 10% — with load transfer + driveline + degressive grip ON. If beta and Fz pass but vx RMSE stays > 0.4 (driveline mismatch) the fix is more driveline physics, NOT a residual. A THIN LEARNED RESIDUAL is justified ONLY if, after load-transfer + driveline + degressive-TMeasy are all in and per-wheel Fz validates < 10%, the lateral/yaw trajectory gap persists (beta@24 p90 in 0.03-0.05 band) — that residual is the unmodeled suspension kinematics/relaxation-length, and it should be a small Fz-and-slip-conditioned correction on fy_rear/fy_front, fit on the SAME telemetry, never a black-box on the full state. Run the existing test_gpu_surrogate.py parity test in a backward-compatible mode (h_cg=0 / static-load fallback path) so the numpy bit-faithfulness contract (tests/test_gpu_surrogate.py) is preserved when transfer is disabled.
